findings.title: The question weighs several factors at once
findings.message: Answering this weighs several separate factors to reach one answer.
findings.hint: Ask one question per factor and combine them in code, where you can see and change the weights. One answer carrying several judgements means less, and you cannot tell which factor moved it. Measured on decision-v7's policy cases: joining a second condition that every case already satisfies, so the right answer does not change, still took the answers from 15 of 20 to 11 of 20 and more than doubled the Brier score, and splitting it recovered all of it. That is the largest cost measured for any check here. Accept it where the factors always move together, so no material can satisfy one and not the others, or where the caller wants the blended judgement and will never read the parts: a severity rubric that composites how bad and how urgent is the documented shape, not a defect.
findings.suggest: Ask one question per factor and weight them in code, so you can see which factor moved the answer. For example, a question about whether to interview someone becomes one about experience, one about the skills the role needs, and one about availability.
findings.evidence: Read: "Does this text read as if it was generated by an AI system rather than written by a person?"

findings.title: Noul does not say what yes and no mean
findings.message: The question carries no criteria, so where the line between yes and no falls is left to the model.
findings.hint: The instruction is enough for many Nouls. Where the boundary is subtle, saying what a yes and a no mean is what moves a question from guessing to deciding.
findings.suggest: Add a `criteria` object with a `true` and a `false` description, saying which material counts as each.

findings.title: A yes/no question about a matter of degree
findings.message: This asks yes or no about something that comes in degrees, and never says where the cut-off falls.
findings.hint: State the cut-off, or ask a Score instead. A Noul at 0.5 means yes and no are equally likely, not that the answer is halfway. Measured on decision-v7's policy cases and on boolq: the defect is detected and the answers do not move. That is the hardest material available here, and a defect that costs nothing measurable is worth reading rather than failing a build over, so this is advice. Accept it where the boundary is one the reader already shares - a legal threshold, a published service level - so naming it in the question would repeat what the material already settles.
findings.suggest: Say where the cut-off falls, or ask a Score over described levels instead. For example, asking whether someone is strong at a language becomes asking whether the CV states they used it at work.
findings.evidence: Read: "Does this text read as if it was generated by an AI system rather than written by a person?"

findings.title: Two questions ask for the same judgement: `slop_bare` and `slop_def`
findings.message: Two questions in this query ask for the same judgement in different words.
findings.hint: Both answers cost a question and move together, so the second buys nothing, and where they disagree the disagreement is noise rather than information. Accept it where the two questions are asked of different parts of the state, so the same words are a different question each time.
findings.suggest: Keep the one whose answer your code acts on and drop the other. Where the two are meant to differ, make the difference explicit in both.
findings.evidence: Both ask: "Is this text an example of AI slop - low … fort machine-style writing?" / "Definition: AI slop is low-quality, gene … text an example of AI slop?"

findings.title: Choice has no fallback option
findings.message: None of the options is an `other` or `none of the above`.
findings.hint: Without a catch-all the probability mass has nowhere to go, so it lands on the nearest wrong label. Measured on decision-v7: where the answer was none of the options, removing the catch-all put a mean 0.79 on a label that could not be right and cost a Brier score of 0.660 against 0.349 with it. Where the answer was among the options it cost nothing.
findings.suggest: Add `"other": "Anything the other options do not cover"`.
